quests.title: The Recollector's Path

dialogue.t: You look much happier than when last we spoke. Seems things have gone well?
Hmm. From what I've learned doing these tasks, I have grown. For now...
You are worthy of being called Bloomguard?
No... not yet. There is still a final portion of the task that I need to complete.
Until all the tasks are done, until your respect is earned, I am not finished. Only then can the "Twin-Horned Chaplet" truly belong to me.
Oh? Looks like you're actually beyond your rebellious phase after all, just as was claimed.
E—Elder, you... still remember that? Forget, I beg of you!
Haha. Regardless, it's good to see that your spirits have returned.
{NICKNAME}. Paimon. Please be witnesses to the truth of whether Sorush is worthy of the Twin-Horned Chaplet.
Then I will await you at the end. See you soon.
The Tunigi Hollow... this was the epicenter of the disaster. Though all seems calm...

dialogue.sit: It's not hard to think of how things were then.

dialogue.t: These crystals are huge... A lot bigger than even Wenut! And to think it's Sorush's responsibility to handle future problems here...
Is this not the most essential duty a Bloomguard should uphold? In addition, Sorush should also expect this of herself.
That's what they say, anyway...
Do you not trust me? Hmph. I did not realize I was at the stage that even the Pale Floater thinks so little of me.
Whoa, Sorush's arrogance makes its grand return!

dialogue.sit: Not sure if that's a good thing or a bad thing.

dialogue.t: Hmph. Why do both of you still harbor such doubt in me after our time together? My pride has never been born of blind arrogance.
Hmm. You should be well aware that I fully understand my past mistakes.
Before, I placed reputation above action, but now, as I have learned, this is an act of purest neglect.
Just as Simurgh became the divine bird through her sacrifice, I will become the Bloomguard by my deeds and hear my name rightfully sung in praise of my service.
Additionally, I have completed all the assignments you have given me, Elder. Now, even you must admit that I am one worthy of the title of Bloomguard, worthy of the Twin-Horned Chaplet.
I indeed have no objection to the choice made by the Khvarena.
What? Did you expect me to object?
No... I merely... did not expect you to agree so easily, Elder...

dialogue.sit: I expected a few rough words at least?

dialogue.t: Ah, I'm not nearly so vicious.
About the responsibilities of a Bloomguard... I did not actually gain any knowledge from the Chaplet...
Is this because I still do not embody the traits of the Bloomguard fully? Do I still lack training?
For this... The title of Bloomguard might be inherited, but the duties are always variable...
I see.
To state it simply: there are no fixed rules, and even more, there are no specific judging standards. Usually, the Khvarena's choice is final.
Huh? So, you're saying...
I will not be taking the Twin-Horned Chaplet from you.

dialogue.sit: Now you don't need to worry about the top of your head getting cold.

dialogue.t: Missing the point!
I understand! This must be part of the test!
Seems like Sorush is having an epiphany...
You are a forgetful one, Pale Floater. I just said it! To pass these tests, besides competence and observation, the most important thing is understanding my past mistakes.

Even if the outcome was already determined, would it not be retreading the path of folly if I cast aside all that I have learned during training? So, I think this must be the last test my elder has left me.
To a worthy Bloomguard this is but a simple task. This is a sign of your complete trust in me, Elder.
I didn't expect you to see right through me. The Khvarena chose well.
But your changes... I suppose {NICKNAME} and Paimon bear some credit for that.
Indeed! My esteemed Yasnapati and the Pale Floater are both beings of merit.
Though I wish to say that I am potent enough alone... I believe that with their aid, the extinguishing of the Sign of Apaosha will be no difficult task.
How very reliable. Don't forget, Mihir and Rashnu will also be able to assist you.
Worry not, Elder! Leave everything to me!
Paimon keeps thinking that Zurvan might have planned this... But seeing Sorush this happy, Paimon can't really complain.
The Tunigi Hollow from before... the epicenter of the disaster of years past...
Wow! Paimon didn't think Sorush would really be able to extinguish the Sign of Apaosha and solve all the trouble happening here...
Extinguishing the Sign of Apaosha is but the duty of the Bloomguard. Sorush only did as she should.

dialogue.sit: It was all thanks to Mihir and Rashnu's help.

dialogue.t: Yeah. And we put in plenty of work too.
Splendid! It's so nice of you, my Yasnapati and the Pale Floater, to look beyond the person of greatest importance: me.

Of course! As long as I hold my responsibilities close to heart, then my elder need not worry for my sake.

quests.description: The training is approaching its conclusion. Zurvan’s approval is but a step away…
